newsitem.title: HUNGARY: CSOPAK UPS ON HIGHER DIVIDEND PLAN - TRADERS.
newsitem.headline: CSOPAK UPS ON HIGHER DIVIDEND PLAN - TRADERS.

text.p: Shares in Hungarian retail group Csopak bucked a mostly bearish trend on the Budapest bourse and gained more than three and a half percent on plans for an increased dividend, traders said.
Csopak shares opened at 2,960 forints, little below Wednesday's closing level of 2,975 and at 1045 GMT, when the last deal was done, they traded at 3,080 forints.
"The rise is clearly the result of the higher dividend ratio," one trader said. "This is so, despite the fact that the dividend ratio is below the inflation."
Csopak's management said on Wednesday it would propose the payout of a 10 percent or 100 forints per share dividend on the 1996 results compared to an eight percent dividend on the 1995 results.
Hungary had an average inflation of 23.6 percent in 1996 and targets an inflation of around 17 percent for 1997.
Csopak will hold its annual shareholders meeting on April 26.
